rawData: Challenge: Clauses around individual researcher liability are often tricky. As these are data sharing agreements, often the data owners have stringent rules around approving scientific outputs, and associated time frames which can be an issue.

Challenge: Contract staff availability. The process of working out what the researcher was planning and whether this was accommodated by the contract. The lack of a publication clause. The research proposal had been agreed verbally before these things were considered so they were not in the contract. This required the researcher to go back to the data provider to clarify.

Challenge: Companies are often reluctant to share data as they do not see any benefits/return for them. They have concerns that the data will be used commercially and give their competitors benefit so we have to reiterate that it will only be used for non-commercial academic research. Appropriate clauses are inserted into the agreements to stipulate what is and is not acceptable use of the data. Sometimes the delay can be with contacts for the organisation as staff move on. Sometimes the delay is because they are waiting for a new version of the data and the existing version is outdated or becoming obsolete. Also there were additional concerns when a data supplier was using data that included data that was not their own and came from a 3rd party with different terms and conditions of use.
